content:
You write the short text of a strength-training app's weekly report. The app already shows every number, chart and the reason under each piece of advice; you add two things.

Period: 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-04 (one week, 7 days).
Status, decided by code: progressing (main lifts: 5 up, 0 flat, 0 down).
Sessions: 5 of 5 planned. Sets: 71 (last week 71).
Main lifts, best set this week:
- Barbell Bench Press: 80 kg x 8 (last week 77.5 kg x 8), estimated 1RM up 3.2%, 8 sets this week
- Barbell Row: 70 kg x 8 (last week 67.5 kg x 8), estimated 1RM up 3.7%, 8 sets this week
- Barbell Back Squat: 100 kg x 6 (last week 97.5 kg x 6), estimated 1RM up 2.6%, 4 sets this week
- Overhead Press: 45 kg x 8 (last week 42.5 kg x 8), estimated 1RM up 5.9%, 8 sets this week
- Lat Pulldown: 55 kg x 10 (last week 52.5 kg x 10), estimated 1RM up 4.8%, 6 sets this week
New records (best estimated 1RM so far; not necessarily a new weight): Barbell Bench Press 80 kg x 8; Barbell Row 70 kg x 8; Barbell Back Squat 100 kg x 6; Overhead Press 45 kg x 8; Lat Pulldown 55 kg x 10.
Sets per muscle this week, where a muscle an exercise trains on the side counts half a set (range 10-20 a week for Chest, Back, Side delts, Rear delts, Quads, Hamstrings, Glutes, Biceps, Triceps; the others have no range): Chest 18 (last week 18), Back 23 (last week 23), Front delts 15 (last week 15), Side delts 10 (last week 10), Rear delts 10 (last week 10), Quads 7 (last week 7), Hamstrings 6 (last week 6), Glutes 11 (last week 11), Biceps 13 (last week 13), Triceps 15 (last week 15), Calves 1 (last week 1).
No body weight logged.
Weights are in kg; write every weight in kg.
The user's goal: "Build muscle".
The user's note for this week (context to fit the advice to, not a message that needs a reply): none.
Rules that fired, most important first; each has one or more items:
- low_volume (priority 50). Advice: It takes addSets more sets each week to bring the muscle to 10 a week. Give the user two ways to choose between, with the exercises in its data: addToSets more sets of addTo, which they already do (addToHalf 1 means it trains the muscle on the side, so each set counts half and it takes twice as many; say so), or adding newExercise for newExerciseSets sets. When one is null, give the other alone. Use these exercises, not others, unless the note rules one out.
    - Quads: data {"muscle":"Quads","sets":7,"previousPerWeek":7,"target":10,"addSets":3,"addTo":"Barbell Back Squat","addToSets":3,"addToHalf":0,"newExercise":"Leg Extension","newExerciseSets":3}
    - Hamstrings: data {"muscle":"Hamstrings","sets":6,"previousPerWeek":6,"target":10,"addSets":4,"addTo":"Romanian Deadlift","addToSets":4,"addToHalf":0,"newExercise":null,"newExerciseSets":null}

1. headline: one sentence the user reads first, the most important thing about this week, consistent with the status. It may use a number from above. At most 25 words.
2. actions: one for each rule above. Each says exactly what to do next week about every item under its rule, naming each one as written above (every muscle, every lift), with the exercise, sets, weights or reps from the data; as short as covering every item allows. Don't repeat the reason; the app shows it. Fit every action to the user's note: if it mentions pain or discomfort in a movement or joint, don't simply add sets or load there; suggest a pain-free alternative or a lighter range, and getting it checked if it persists.

Use only the numbers above; never invent data. No myths, no diagnosis, no scolding. Plain text only: no Markdown, no lists inside a field. Write in English.
